observation_summary: Entity graph run: 2 filings, 75 directors, 7 proposals, 23 signals. Status ok. 19 of 23 signals (83%) were high_trust_director — dominated by a config parameter (HighTrustMinFilings) that was defined and documented but never enforced in the signal scoring code.
actions_taken: Identified that HighTrustMinFilings was a dead config key: documented in Rules, present in entity-graph-rules.json, but scoreOneDirector only checked ApprovalPct >= HighTrustMinApproval without any filing-history gate. This caused 19 high_trust_director signals in a 2-filing batch, making up 83% of all signals and drowning out actionable adverse signals. Fix: (1) Added FilterHighTrustByMinFilings() to signals.go — filters high_trust_director signals for directors whose per-ticker filing count in the graph is below the configured minimum; count is ticker-scoped so cross-board appearances at other companies don't count. (2) Wired the filter into cmd/entity-graph/main.go immediately after ScoreDirectorVotes inside the per-filing loop. (3) Raised high_trust_min_filings from 1 to 2 in config/entity-graph-rules.json so directors now require 2 proxy season appearances at the same ticker before receiving a high_trust signal. (4) Added 5 new unit tests covering first-filing suppression, return-director pass-through, ticker-scoped counting, non-high-trust signal preservation, and no-op at minFilings=1. All go test ./... pass.
notes: The governance_peer_underperformer signal for BEN (score 0.29, high severity) is correct and actionable — BEN's governance health is 29 points below its financial sector median. No parser changes needed: observation gaps=null. The HighTrustMinFilings=2 change takes effect on the next entity-graph batch without a process restart (rules are hot-reloaded per runBatch). Existing high_trust signals in signals.ndjson from prior runs are not retroactively removed — only new batch processing is affected.
